newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank says bank spreads lower.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank says bank spreads lower.

text.p: Banks' spreads in the Philippines had become lower due to the drop in lending rates and increase in deposit rates arising from the increased competition in the industry, Philippine Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said in a statement on Friday.

Banks spreads, measured as the difference between the lending rate and the weighted average interest expense on savings and time deposits, averaged at 6.38 percent in the first nine months of the year, lower than the 1990 average of 11.243 percent, Singson said.

The average lending rate had declined continuously over the years to 14.219 percent as of September 1996 from 24.32 percent in 1990 on account of steps made by the Central Bank to reduce reserve requirements and slow down inflation, the statement said.
